summary: this is the object a method or constructor is running on. Inside a class, this.name is the object's field, and a plain name is a local variable or a parameter.
notes: In BrokenStudent, name = name; assigns the parameter to itself. The fields are never created, so they print as undefined.
this.name = name; copies the parameter into the object's field.
In maya.setGpa(3.9), this is maya, so this.gpa changes maya's field.
pitfall: Copying a method out of its object, as in const update = maya.setGpa; update(4.0);, causes TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'gpa'). Called that way, this is undefined.
contrast: JavaScript always writes this.field, like Python's self.field, even when no parameter has the same name. Unlike both, this is set by how a method is called: maya.setGpa() sets it to maya, but a copied method loses it.
